symptom: PC-A cannot ping PC-B on the same switch. Both are assigned to VLAN 10 but connectivity fails.
topology_note: 2x PCs connected to a Cisco 2960 switch. PC-A on Fa0/1, PC-B on Fa0/2. Both supposed to be in VLAN 10.
show_outputs:
Switch# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2
10   SALES                            active    
Switch# show interfaces Fa0/1 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1
expected_fault: Ports Fa0/1 and Fa0/2 are assigned to VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10.

symptom: All PCs in the building cannot obtain an IP address automatically. Static IPs work fine.
topology_note: Cisco 2811 router as DHCP server. LAN 192.168.1.0/24. PCs on Fa0/0.
show_outputs:
Router# show ip dhcp pool
Pool LAN_POOL :
 Network: 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0
 DNS Server: 8.8.8.8
Router# show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL
 network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0
 dns-server 8.8.8.8
expected_fault: DHCP pool is missing the default-router (gateway) statement.

symptom: Remote branch office (192.168.3.0/24) cannot reach HQ (192.168.1.0/24). Local LAN works fine.
show_outputs:
R2# show ip route
C    10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0
C    192.168.3.0/24 is directly connected, FastEthernet0/0
R2# show running-config | section router rip
router rip
 version 2
 network 10.0.0.0
expected_fault: R2 RIP config missing network 192.168.3.0 statement so HQ never learns the branch network.

symptom: Server in DMZ (192.168.2.10) is completely unreachable from the internet-facing interface.
topology_note: Perimeter router: Gi0/0 outside (203.0.113.1/30) Gi0/1 inside Gi0/2 DMZ (192.168.2.1/24). Extended ACL on Gi0/0 inbound.
show_outputs:
Router# show ip access-lists OUTSIDE_IN
Extended IP access list OUTSIDE_IN
    10 deny ip any host 192.168.2.10 (1482 matches)
    20 permit ip any any
Router# show ip interface Gi0/0
  Inbound  access list is OUTSIDE_IN
expected_fault: ACL OUTSIDE_IN has explicit deny blocking all traffic to DMZ server before the permit rule.

symptom: Trunk link between two switches shows only VLAN 1 traffic. VLANs 10 20 30 are dark.
topology_note: Two Cisco 3560 switches on Gi0/1 trunk. SW1 has VLANs 10 20 30. SW2 should route them via SVIs.
show_outputs:
SW2# show vlan brief
VLAN Name     Status    Ports
1    default   active    Gi0/2
SW2# show interfaces Gi0/1 trunk
Port        Vlans in spanning tree forwarding state and not pruned
Gi0/1       1
expected_fault: VLANs 10 20 30 not created on SW2 so STP prunes them from the trunk leaving only VLAN 1.

symptom: All users report internet is down. Pinging ISP gateway (8.8.8.8) from router fails.
topology_note: Edge router: Gi0/0 to ISP (DHCP) Gi0/1 LAN 192.168.100.1/24. ISP gateway 203.0.113.254.
show_outputs:
Router# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set
C    192.168.100.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1
C    203.0.113.252/30 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
Router# show running-config | include ip route
expected_fault: No default route configured — gateway of last resort is not set.
concept: Default Route / Gateway of Last Resort

symptom: VoIP phones on VLAN 20 cannot register with call manager. Data PCs on VLAN 10 work fine.
topology_note: Access switch. Ports Fa0/5-Fa0/12 should carry data VLAN 10 and voice VLAN 20.
show_outputs:
Switch# show interfaces Fa0/5 switchport
Access Mode VLAN: 10
Voice VLAN: none
Switch# show vlan brief
VLAN Name     Status    Ports
10   DATA      active    Fa0/5
20   VOICE     active
expected_fault: Voice VLAN 20 exists but is not assigned to access ports using switchport voice vlan command.

symptom: IPsec VPN tunnel between branch and HQ shows as down. WAN pings between routers work.
topology_note: Site-to-site IPsec VPN. HQ at 10.0.0.1 Branch at 10.0.0.2. IKEv1 Phase 1 failing.
show_outputs:
Branch# show crypto isakmp sa
10.0.0.1   10.0.0.2   MM_NO_STATE   1001   ACTIVE (deleted)
Branch# show crypto isakmp policy
encryption: AES-256
HQ# show crypto isakmp policy
encryption: 3DES
expected_fault: IKEv1 Phase 1 fails: encryption mismatch — Branch proposes AES-256 but HQ is configured for 3DES.

symptom: New switch added to network. Connected uplink port shows as err-disabled immediately.
topology_note: New Cisco 2960 connected to distribution switch Gi1/0/24. Port security was configured on that port.
show_outputs:
Distribution# show interfaces Gi1/0/24 status
Gi1/0/24   err-disabled
Distribution# show port-security interface Gi1/0/24
Port Status: Secure-shutdown
Violation Mode: Shutdown
Maximum MAC Addresses: 1
Security Violation Count: 1
expected_fault: Port security violation triggered by new switch MAC address causing err-disabled state.

symptom: Inter-VLAN routing stopped after switch reboot. Router-on-a-stick was working before.
topology_note: R1 with sub-interfaces Fa0/0.10 and Fa0/0.20 for inter-VLAN routing connected to switch trunk port.
show_outputs:
R1# show interfaces Fa0/0
FastEthernet0/0 is administratively down, line protocol is down
R1# show interfaces Fa0/0.10
FastEthernet0/0.10 is up, line protocol is up
R1# show running-config | section interface Fa0/0
interface FastEthernet0/0
 no ip address
 shutdown
expected_fault: Parent interface Fa0/0 is administratively shut down taking all sub-interfaces down with it.

symptom: OSPF neighbors not forming between R1 and R2. Both routers show OSPF running.
topology_note: R1 (10.1.1.1/24) and R2 (10.1.1.2/24) connected on same Ethernet. Both running OSPF area 0.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID  Pri  State  Dead Time  Address  Interface
R1# show ip ospf interface Fa0/0
 Timer intervals configured, Hello 10, Dead 40
R2# show ip ospf interface Fa0/0
 Timer intervals configured, Hello 5, Dead 20
expected_fault: OSPF hello/dead timer mismatch — R1 uses Hello 10 / Dead 40 but R2 uses Hello 5 / Dead 20.

symptom: EIGRP routes missing from routing table. Two routers directly connected but no EIGRP neighbor.
topology_note: R1 and R2 directly connected via Fa0/0. Both configured for EIGRP AS 100.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip eigrp neighbors
IP-EIGRP neighbors for process 100
R2# show running-config | section router eigrp
router eigrp 200
 network 10.0.0.0
expected_fault: EIGRP AS number mismatch — R1 runs AS 100 but R2 runs AS 200. Neighbors require matching AS numbers.

symptom: Serial link between two routers is down. Both DCE and DTE configured.
topology_note: R1 (DCE) Se0/0 connected to R2 (DTE) Se0/0. PPP encapsulation on both ends.
show_outputs:
R1# show interfaces Se0/0
Serial0/0 is up, line protocol is down
 Encapsulation PPP
R2# show interfaces Se0/0
Serial0/0 is up, line protocol is down
 Encapsulation HDLC
R1# show running-config | section interface Se0/0
interface Serial0/0
 encapsulation ppp
expected_fault: Encapsulation mismatch — R1 uses PPP but R2 uses HDLC. Both ends must match.

symptom: New PC gets IP from DHCP but cannot reach anything outside its subnet.
topology_note: Router as DHCP server. Pool for 192.168.5.0/24. Router Fa0/0 = 192.168.5.1/24.
show_outputs:
Router# show ip dhcp pool
Pool OFFICE :
 Network: 192.168.5.0 255.255.255.0
 Default router: 192.168.5.254
Router# show interfaces Fa0/0
FastEthernet0/0 is up
 Internet address is 192.168.5.1/24
expected_fault: DHCP pool default-router (192.168.5.254) does not match the actual router interface IP (192.168.5.1). Clients get wrong gateway.

symptom: Two PCs on same switch cause intermittent connectivity loss for each other.
topology_note: Two PCs on SW1. PC-A = 192.168.1.10/24. PC-B was mis-configured with same IP 192.168.1.10/24.
show_outputs:
SW1# show mac address-table
Vlan  Mac Address     Type    Ports
1     aabb.cc00.0001  DYNAMIC Fa0/1
1     aabb.cc00.0002  DYNAMIC Fa0/2
Router# show arp
192.168.1.10  aabb.cc00.0001
192.168.1.10  aabb.cc00.0002
%IP-4-DUPADDR: Duplicate address 192.168.1.10 on FastEthernet0/0
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address 192.168.1.10 assigned to two different PCs causing ARP conflicts.

symptom: Users on 192.168.10.0/24 cannot reach server on 192.168.20.0/24 through the router.
topology_note: R1 with Fa0/0 (192.168.10.1/24) and Fa0/1 (192.168.20.1/24). Extended ACL on Fa0/0 outbound.
show_outputs:
Router# show ip access-lists BLOCK_INTER
Extended IP access list BLOCK_INTER
    10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 (230 matches)
    20 permit ip any any
Router# show ip interface Fa0/0
  Outbound access list is BLOCK_INTER
expected_fault: ACL BLOCK_INTER explicitly denies traffic from VLAN 10 to VLAN 20 on the outbound interface.

symptom: NAT is configured but inside hosts still appear with private IPs on the outside.
topology_note: R1 as NAT router. Gi0/0 outside (public) Gi0/1 inside (192.168.1.0/24). NAT overload configured.
show_outputs:
Router# show ip nat translations
Router# show running-config | section ip nat
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0 overload
Router# show ip interface Gi0/0
  Outbound access list is not set
Router# show ip interface Gi0/1
  NAT: disabled
expected_fault: NAT inside is not enabled on Gi0/1 — the inside interface has NAT disabled so traffic is not translated.

symptom: SSH to router fails with connection refused. Telnet works fine.
topology_note: Cisco 2811 router. Admin wants SSH-only access. Attempted SSH from PC (192.168.1.100).
show_outputs:
Router# show ip ssh
SSH Disabled - version 1.99
%Please create RSA keys (of at least 768 bits size) to enable SSH v1.99
Router# show running-config | section line vty
line vty 0 4
 password cisco
 login
 transport input telnet
expected_fault: SSH is disabled because RSA keys have not been generated. Crypto key generate rsa is required.

symptom: PC cannot reach default gateway even though it has the correct IP and mask.
topology_note: PC on Fa0/1 of SW1. Default gateway = 192.168.1.1 (router Fa0/0). Router Fa0/0 connected to Fa0/24 of SW1.
show_outputs:
SW1# show interfaces Fa0/24 status
Port    Status       Vlan
Fa0/24  notconnect   1
SW1# show interfaces Fa0/1 status
Port    Status       Vlan
Fa0/1   connected    1
expected_fault: Uplink port Fa0/24 (connecting switch to router) shows notconnect — physical cable is unplugged or faulty.

symptom: Routing table on R2 shows correct routes but traffic still loops between R1 and R2.
topology_note: R1 and R2 in a two-router topology. Static routes configured on both. R1 points to R2 for 10.0.0.0/8 and R2 points to R1 for same.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip route
S    10.0.0.0/8 [1/0] via 192.168.1.2
R2# show ip route
S    10.0.0.0/8 [1/0] via 192.168.1.1
R1# show ip route 10.5.5.5
Routing entry for 10.0.0.0/8
  Known via static, via 192.168.1.2
expected_fault: Routing loop — R1 and R2 each point to the other for 10.0.0.0/8 creating an infinite loop with no exit.

symptom: Spanning tree is blocking the only uplink on an access switch causing total outage.
topology_note: Access switch SW3 connected to distribution SW1 via Fa0/24 (primary) and Fa0/23 (backup). STP blocking Fa0/24.
show_outputs:
SW3# show spanning-tree
VLAN0001
  Root ID Priority 32769 Address aabb.cc00.1111
  Bridge ID Priority 32769 Address aabb.cc00.9999
Interface  Role  Sts  Cost  Prio
Fa0/23     Root  FWD  19    128
Fa0/24     Altn  BLK  19    128
expected_fault: STP elected Fa0/23 as root port and blocked Fa0/24. Primary uplink is blocked — port priority or cost adjustment needed.

symptom: HSRP active router is the lower-priority router causing suboptimal forwarding.
topology_note: Two routers R1 (priority 110) and R2 (priority 90) in HSRP group 1. R1 should be active but R2 is active.
show_outputs:
R1# show standby brief
P indicates configured to preempt.
Interface  Grp  Pri  P  State   Active    Standby
Fa0/0      1    110     Standby 192.168.1.3 local
R2# show standby brief
Interface  Grp  Pri  P  State   Active    Standby
Fa0/0      1    90      Active  local     192.168.1.2
expected_fault: R1 has higher priority (110) but preempt is not configured so R2 remained active after it came up first.

symptom: EtherChannel between two switches is not forming. Individual links are up.
topology_note: SW1 and SW2 connected via Fa0/1 and Fa0/2. LACP EtherChannel configured on both sides.
show_outputs:
SW1# show etherchannel summary
Flags: D-down P-bundled U-in-use
Group  Port-channel  Protocol  Ports
1      Po1(SD)        LACP      Fa0/1(D) Fa0/2(D)
SW1# show running-config | section interface Fa0/1
interface FastEthernet0/1
 channel-group 1 mode passive
SW2# show running-config | section interface Fa0/1
interface FastEthernet0/1
 channel-group 1 mode passive
expected_fault: Both sides configured as LACP passive — at least one side must be active for negotiation to succeed.

symptom: IPv6 hosts on the same link cannot communicate with each other.
topology_note: Two routers R1 and R2 on same Ethernet segment. IPv6 unicast routing enabled. Link-local addresses expected.
show_outputs:
R1# show ipv6 interface Fa0/0
FastEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  IPv6 is enabled, link-local address is FE80::1
  No global unicast address is configured
R2# show ipv6 neighbors
IPv6 Address  Age  Link-layer Addr  State  Interface
R1# ping FE80::1
Output Interface: FastEthernet0/0
!!!!!
expected_fault: No global unicast IPv6 addresses configured — only link-local addresses exist so hosts cannot route beyond the local link.

symptom: BGP neighbor relationship between two ISP routers not establishing.
topology_note: R1 (AS 65001) and R2 (AS 65002) configured for eBGP. Peering on 10.0.0.0/30 link.
show_outputs:
R1# show bgp summary
Neighbor   V  AS    MsgRcvd  MsgSent  Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.0.0.2   4  65002 0        0        never    Active
R1# show running-config | section router bgp
router bgp 65001
 neighbor 10.0.0.2 remote-as 65002
R2# show running-config | section router bgp
router bgp 65002
 neighbor 10.0.0.1 remote-as 65001
R2# show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0  10.0.0.2  YES manual  up  down
expected_fault: R2 Gi0/0 line protocol is down — physical connectivity issue preventing BGP TCP session from establishing.

symptom: DHCP snooping enabled but legitimate DHCP offers are being dropped on access ports.
topology_note: Core switch with DHCP snooping enabled globally. DHCP server connected on Gi0/1. Clients on Fa0/1-Fa0/10.
show_outputs:
Switch# show dhcp snooping
DHCP snooping is configured on following VLANs: 1
Switch# show dhcp snooping binding
Switch# show ip dhcp snooping interface Gi0/1
Interface    Trusted    Rate limit (pps)
Gi0/1        no         15
expected_fault: DHCP server port Gi0/1 is not configured as trusted — DHCP snooping drops all server offers arriving on untrusted ports.

symptom: Users report website names don't resolve but IP address pings work fine.
topology_note: Office LAN. Router as DNS relay. Clients use 192.168.1.1 as DNS server. ISP DNS is 8.8.8.8.
show_outputs:
Router# show running-config | include dns
ip name-server 8.8.8.8
Router# show running-config | section interface Fa0/0
interface FastEthernet0/0
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0
 ip helper-address 192.168.1.1
Router# debug ip dns
DNS: no view dns process running
expected_fault: ip dns server command not configured on router — router cannot answer client DNS queries despite having a name-server set.
concept: DNS Server Not Enabled on Router

symptom: Wireless clients associated to AP but cannot get IP address. Wired clients work fine.
topology_note: Cisco WLC managing lightweight APs. SSID CORP mapped to VLAN 30. DHCP scope for VLAN 30 on router.
show_outputs:
WLC# show interface summary
Interface  VLAN  IP Address        Type
management  1    192.168.1.10/24  Static
CORP_WIFI  30   192.168.30.1/24  Dynamic
Router# show ip dhcp pool
No DHCP pool configured for 192.168.30.0
expected_fault: No DHCP pool configured on the router for the wireless VLAN 30 (192.168.30.0/24). Wireless clients have no IP source.
concept: DHCP Pool Missing for Wireless VLAN

symptom: After adding a new router to OSPF area 1 routes are not being redistributed into area 0.
topology_note: OSPF multi-area. ABR connects area 0 and area 1. New router R3 added to area 1 with loopback 3.3.3.3.
show_outputs:
R3# show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID  State  Interface
1.1.1.1      FULL   Fa0/0
ABR# show ip route ospf
O IA 192.168.1.0/24 [110/2] via 10.0.0.1
ABR# show ip ospf database
R3 loopback not in database
R3# show running-config | section router ospf
router ospf 1
 network 10.1.1.0 0.0.0.255 area 1
expected_fault: R3 loopback 3.3.3.3 not included in any OSPF network statement so it is not advertised into the OSPF domain.

symptom: Inter-VLAN routing works for VLAN 10 but VLAN 20 hosts cannot reach any other network.
topology_note: Layer 3 switch with SVIs. SVI for VLAN 10 (192.168.10.1/24) works. SVI for VLAN 20 (192.168.20.1/24) created but down.
show_outputs:
SW# show interfaces vlan 20
Vlan20 is up, line protocol is down
SW# show vlan brief
VLAN Name     Status    Ports
10   DATA      active    Fa0/1
20   VOICE     active    
SW# show running-config | section interface Vlan20
interface Vlan20
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: SVI VLAN 20 line protocol is down because no active physical port is assigned to VLAN 20 on the switch.

symptom: PPPoE client router cannot connect to ISP. Authentication fails repeatedly.
topology_note: Edge router configured as PPPoE client on Gi0/0. ISP uses CHAP authentication. Username and password set.
show_outputs:
Router# show pppoe session
 SID  RemMAC         LocMAC         Intf  VAccess  State
   1  aabb.cc001122  aabb.cc003344  Gi0/0  Vi1      LCP_LISN
Router# debug ppp authentication
PPP: Phase is AUTHENTICATING
CHAP: O CHALLENGE id 1 len 23 from Router
CHAP: I FAILURE id 1 len 26 msg is Failed
expected_fault: CHAP authentication failing — username or password configured on the router does not match ISP's expected credentials.

symptom: Router has two paths to the destination but always uses the slower serial link.
topology_note: R1 connected to R2 via Fa0/0 (fast) and Se0/0 (slow). Both running OSPF. Fa0/0 should be preferred.
show_outputs:
R1# show ip route 192.168.5.0
Routing entry for 192.168.5.0/24
  Known via ospf, via 10.0.0.2, Serial0/0 cost 64
R1# show ip ospf interface Fa0/0
 Cost: 64
R1# show ip ospf interface Se0/0
 Cost: 64
expected_fault: OSPF cost is identical on both interfaces (64). FastEthernet should have lower cost (1) than Serial. Auto-cost reference-bandwidth may not match link speeds.

symptom: Users in one office building cannot reach users in another building on same campus network.
topology_note: Two buildings connected by fiber. Building A switch (SW-A) uplinks to core via Gi0/1. Same VLAN 50 across both.
show_outputs:
SW-A# show interfaces Gi0/1 trunk
Port  Mode  Encapsulation  Status   Native vlan
Gi0/1 auto  negotiate      not-trunking  1
SW-Core# show interfaces Gi0/1 trunk
Port  Mode  Encapsulation  Status   Native vlan
Gi0/1 on    802.1q         trunking  1
expected_fault: SW-A trunk port is in auto mode but SW-Core is in on mode — DTP will not negotiate a trunk when one side is on and the other is auto.

symptom: Network admin locked out of router after applying a new ACL.
topology_note: Router with ACL applied to VTY lines to restrict management access. Admin applied wrong source IP.
show_outputs:
Router# show running-config | section line vty
line vty 0 4
 access-class MGMT_ACCESS in
 login local
 transport input ssh
Router# show ip access-lists MGMT_ACCESS
Extended IP access list MGMT_ACCESS
    10 permit tcp host 10.10.10.99 any eq 22
    20 deny ip any any (implicit)
expected_fault: ACL MGMT_ACCESS only permits SSH from 10.10.10.99 — admin is connecting from a different IP so they are blocked by the implicit deny.

symptom: Multicast video stream not reaching receivers even though PIM is configured.
topology_note: Multicast source at 239.1.1.1. Receivers on multiple VLANs. PIM sparse-mode on all router interfaces.
show_outputs:
Router# show ip pim neighbor
Router# show ip mroute 239.1.1.1
(*, 239.1.1.1), uptime 00:05:10, sparse-mode
  Incoming interface: Null
  Outgoing interface list: Null
Router# show running-config | include ip multicast-routing
expected_fault: ip multicast-routing command is missing from global config — PIM neighbors and mroute entries cannot form without it.
